about.text: Glycomacropeptide (GMP) is a glycosylated peptide formed during renneting as a fragment of sweet whey. Acid whey from yogurt or curdling cheese without the use of rennet does not contain GMP. The unglycosylated form is known as caseinomacropeptide or CMP. Both forms exist in roughly similar amounts in whey.

facts.v: Chymosin (rennet) cuts κ-casein between residues 105 and 106; GMP = residues 106–169 (64 amino acids, about 7 kDa) goes into the whey
GMP has none of its own; commercial GMP still carries about 5 mg Phe/g from leftover whey protein, pilot polishing got 4.7 down to 2.7 mg/g
About 52 % in the pilot process (purity chosen over yield)
